candidate.answerReason: If p is the whole-dollar full price and f is the full-price count, then p(140+f)=4002. The count bounds force 15≤p≤28, and 23 is the only divisor of 4002 in that interval. Thus f=34 and the full-price revenue is 23×34=$782.

methods.label: Bound the price and use divisibility
methods.explanation:
The full price is a whole number of dollars, so clearing the half-price denominator will let us use integer factors. Let \(p\) be the positive integer full price and \(f\) the number of full-price tickets. Then \(140-f\) tickets sell for \(p/2\) dollars each, giving
\[
pf+\frac p2(140-f)=2001.
\]
Doubling and combining terms gives
\[
p(140+f)=4002.
\]
Since \(0\le f\le140\), we have \(140\le140+f\le280\). Consequently,
\[
\frac{4002}{280}\le p\le\frac{4002}{140}.
\]
Because \(p\) is an integer, \(15\le p\le28\).

Also, \(p\) must divide
\[
4002=2\cdot3\cdot23\cdot29.
\]
A divisor in the required interval cannot contain \(29\). Without \(23\), it would be at most \(2\cdot3=6\); with \(23\), any additional prime factor would make it exceed \(28\). Thus the only possible price is \(p=23\).

It follows that
\[
f=\frac{4002}{23}-140=174-140=34.
\]
This is a valid ticket count, leaving \(106\) half-price tickets. The full-price tickets raised
\[
23\cdot34=782
\]
dollars, so the answer is \(\$782\), choice A.
